claim: Serotonin neurons of the dorsal and median raphe nuclei (DR, MR) collectively innervate the entire forebrain and midbrain.
source: Serotonin neurons of the dorsal and median raphe nuclei (DR, MR) collectively innervate the entire forebrain and midbrain, modulating diverse physiology and behavior.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about serotonin neuron projections.

claim: Plate-based single-cell RNA-sequencing was used to generate a comprehensive dataset comprising eleven transcriptomically distinct serotonin neuron clusters.
source: To gain a fundamental understanding of their molecular heterogeneity, we used plate-based single-cell RNA-sequencing to generate a comprehensive dataset comprising eleven transcriptomically distinct serotonin neuron clusters.
evidence: The methods and results are described in the manuscript, including Figure 1.

claim: Systematic in situ hybridization mapped specific clusters to the principal DR, caudal DR, or MR.
source: Systematic in situ hybridization mapped specific clusters to the principal DR, caudal DR, or MR.
evidence: This is supported by the HCR-smFISH experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: DR serotonin neurons co-expressing vesicular glutamate transporter-3 preferentially innervate the cortex.
source: Whole-brain axonal projection mapping revealed that DR serotonin neurons co-expressing vesicular glutamate transporter-3 preferentially innervate the cortex, whereas those co-expressing thyrotropin-releasing hormone innervate subcortical regions in particular the hypothalamus.
evidence: This is demonstrated through whole-brain imaging experiments shown in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: DR serotonin neurons co-expressing thyrotropin-releasing hormone innervate subcortical regions in particular the hypothalamus.
source: Whole-brain axonal projection mapping revealed that DR serotonin neurons co-expressing vesicular glutamate transporter-3 preferentially innervate the cortex, whereas those co-expressing thyrotropin-releasing hormone innervate subcortical regions in particular the hypothalamus.
evidence: This is demonstrated through whole-brain imaging experiments shown in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: Reconstruction of 50 individual DR serotonin neurons revealed diverse and segregated axonal projection patterns at the single-cell level.
source: Reconstruction of 50 individual DR serotonin neurons revealed diverse and segregated axonal projection patterns at the single-cell level.
evidence: This is supported by the fMOST imaging and reconstruction data shown in Figure 8.

claim: Serotonin is a phylogenetically ancient signaling molecule.
source: Serotonin is a phylogenetically ancient signaling molecule (Hay-Schmidt, 2000) and the most widely distributed neuromodulator in the brain (Dahlström and Fuxe, 1964; Steinbusch, 1981).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hay-Schmidt, 2000.

claim: Serotonin is the most widely distributed neuromodulator in the brain.
source: Serotonin is a phylogenetically ancient signaling molecule (Hay-Schmidt, 2000) and the most widely distributed neuromodulator in the brain (Dahlström and Fuxe, 1964; Steinbusch, 1981).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dahlström and Fuxe, 1964; Steinbusch, 1981.

claim: The serotonin system innervates nearly every region of the brain.
source: The serotonin system innervates nearly every region of the brain (Jacobs and Azmitia, 1992), even though it only constitutes ~1/200,000 of all CNS neurons in humans.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jacobs and Azmitia, 1992.

claim: The serotonin system constitutes approximately 1/200,000 of all CNS neurons in humans.
source: The serotonin system innervates nearly every region of the brain (Jacobs and Azmitia, 1992), even though it only constitutes ~1/200,000 of all CNS neurons in humans.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact about the proportion of serotonin neurons.

claim: The serotonin system is critically involved in a broad range of brain functions.
source: It is critically involved in a broad range of brain functions and is the most frequently targeted neural system pharmacologically for treating psychiatric disorders (Belmaker and Agam, 2008; Ravindran and Stein, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Belmaker and Agam, 2008; Ravindran and Stein, 2010.

claim: The serotonin system is the most frequently targeted neural system pharmacologically for treating psychiatric disorders.
source: It is critically involved in a broad range of brain functions and is the most frequently targeted neural system pharmacologically for treating psychiatric disorders (Belmaker and Agam, 2008; Ravindran and Stein, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Belmaker and Agam, 2008; Ravindran and Stein, 2010.

claim: Serotonin neurons in the central nervous system are spatially clustered in the brainstem, originally designated as groups B1–B9.
source: Serotonin neurons in the central nervous system are spatially clustered in the brainstem, originally designated as groups B1–B9 (Dahlström and Fuxe, 1964).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dahlström and Fuxe, 1964.

claim: Groups B1–B3 are located in the medulla and provide descending serotonergic innervation to the spinal cord and other parts of the medulla.
source: Groups B1–B3 are located in the medulla and provide descending serotonergic innervation to the spinal cord and other parts of the medulla.
evidence: This is stated as established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Groups B4–B9 are located in the pons and midbrain, including the dorsal raphe (DR; groups B6 and B7) and median raphe (MR; groups B5 and B8) nucleus.
source: Groups B4–B9 are located in the pons and midbrain, including the dorsal raphe (DR; groups B6 and B7) and median raphe (MR; groups B5 and B8) nucleus, and provide ascending innervation to the forebrain and midbrain.
evidence: This is stated as established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Groups B4–B9 provide ascending innervation to the forebrain and midbrain.
source: Groups B4–B9 are located in the pons and midbrain, including the dorsal raphe (DR; groups B6 and B7) and median raphe (MR; groups B5 and B8) nucleus, and provide ascending innervation to the forebrain and midbrain.
evidence: This is stated as established anatomical knowledge.

claim: The DR and MR serotonin systems have been linked with the regulation of many mental states and processes, including anxiety, mood, impulsivity, aggression, learning, reward, social interaction.
source: The DR and MR serotonin systems have been linked with the regulation of many mental states and processes, including anxiety, mood, impulsivity, aggression, learning, reward, social interaction, and hence remain the focus of intense research (Deneris and Wyler, 2012; Olivier, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Deneris and Wyler, 2012; Olivier, 2015.

claim: The DR and MR serotonin systems differ in developmental origin, connectivity, physiology, and behavioral function.
source: Evidence has suggested that the DR and MR serotonin systems differ in developmental origin, connectivity, physiology, and behavioral function (Alonso et al., 2013; Calizo et al., 2011; Okaty et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Alonso et al., 2013; Calizo et al., 2011; Okaty et al., 2019.

claim: DR serotonin neurons derive entirely from rhombomere 1 of the developing mouse brain.
source: DR serotonin neurons derive entirely from rhombomere 1 of the developing mouse brain, whereas MR serotonin neurons derive predominantly from rhombomeres 1, 2, and 3 (Alonso et al., 2013; Bang et al., 2012; Jensen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Alonso et al., 2013; Bang et al., 2012; Jensen et al., 2008.

claim: MR serotonin neurons derive predominantly from rhombomeres 1, 2, and 3.
source: DR serotonin neurons derive entirely from rhombomere 1 of the developing mouse brain, whereas MR serotonin neurons derive predominantly from rhombomeres 1, 2, and 3 (Alonso et al., 2013; Bang et al., 2012; Jensen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Alonso et al., 2013; Bang et al., 2012; Jensen et al., 2008.

claim: The DR and MR receive similar inputs globally from specific brain regions.
source: Although the DR and MR receive similar inputs globally from specific brain regions (Ogawa et al., 2014; Pollak Dorocic et al., 2014; Weissbourd et al., 2014), they project to largely complementary forebrain targets.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ogawa et al., 2014; Pollak Dorocic et al., 2014; Weissbourd et al., 2014.

claim: The DR and MR project to largely complementary forebrain targets.
source: Although the DR and MR receive similar inputs globally from specific brain regions (Ogawa et al., 2014; Pollak Dorocic et al., 2014; Weissbourd et al., 2014), they project to largely complementary forebrain targets.
evidence: This is stated as a known difference between DR and MR projections.

claim: The MR serotonin neurons project to structures near the midline.
source: The MR serotonin neurons project to structures near the midline, whereas the DR serotonin neurons target more lateral regions (Jacobs and Azmitia, 1992; Muzerelle et al., 2016; Vertes, 1991; Vertes et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jacobs and Azmitia, 1992; Muzerelle et al., 2016; Vertes, 1991; Vertes et al., 1999.

claim: The DR serotonin neurons target more lateral regions.
source: The MR serotonin neurons project to structures near the midline, whereas the DR serotonin neurons target more lateral regions (Jacobs and Azmitia, 1992; Muzerelle et al., 2016; Vertes, 1991; Vertes et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jacobs and Azmitia, 1992; Muzerelle et al., 2016; Vertes, 1991; Vertes et al., 1999.

claim: Serotonin neurons in the MR and DR have different electrophysiological characteristics, such as resting potential, membrane resistance, and reaction to serotonin receptor-1A agonist.
source: Slice physiology recording showed that the serotonin neurons in the MR and DR have different ﻿electrophysiological ﻿characteristics, such as resting potential, membrane resistance, and reaction to serotonin receptor-1A agonist (Calizo et al., 2011; Fernandez et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Calizo et al., 2011; Fernandez et al., 2016.

claim: Activation of the DR and MR has been suggested to mediate opposing roles in emotional regulation.
source: Finally, activation of these two raphe nuclei has been suggested to mediate opposing roles in emotional regulation (Teissier et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Teissier et al., 2015.

claim: MR serotonin neurons arising from different cell lineages are anatomically mixed in the adult.
source: Although MR serotonin neurons arising from different cell lineages are anatomically mixed in the adult, they have distinct electrophysiological properties (Okaty et al., 2015) and potentially distinct behavioral functions (Kim et al., 2009; Okaty et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Okaty et al., 2015.

claim: MR serotonin neurons arising from different cell lineages have distinct electrophysiological properties.
source: Although MR serotonin neurons arising from different cell lineages are anatomically mixed in the adult, they have distinct electrophysiological properties (Okaty et al., 2015) and potentially distinct behavioral functions (Kim et al., 2009; Okaty et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Okaty et al., 2015.

claim: There are subgroup-specific projection patterns within the DR serotonin system.
source: Accumulating evidence indicates that there are subgroup-specific projection patterns within the DR serotonin system (Niederkofler et al., 2016; Ren et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Niederkofler et al., 2016; Ren et al., 2018.

claim: The electrophysiological properties of DR serotonin neurons vary according to the projection patterns.
source: The electrophysiological properties of DR serotonin neurons vary according to the projection patterns (Fernandez et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fernandez et al., 2016.

claim: DR serotonin neurons that project to frontal cortex and amygdala constitute two sub-systems with distinct cell body locations, axonal collateralization patterns, biased inputs, physiological response properties, and behavioral functions.
source: As a specific example, we recently found that DR serotonin neurons that project to frontal cortex and amygdala constitute two sub-systems with distinct cell body locations, axonal collateralization patterns, biased inputs, physiological response properties, and behavioral functions (Ren et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ren et al., 2018.

claim: Nearly all 999 neurons expressed the genes encoding tryptophan hydroxylase 2 (Tph2), transcription factor Pet1 (Fev), the plasma membrane serotonin transporter (Sert), and vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (Vmat2).
source: The data quality and serotonin identity were validated by the fact that nearly all 999 neurons expressed the genes encoding: (1) tryptophan hydroxylase 2 (Tph2), a key enzyme for serotonin biosynthesis; (2) transcription factor Pet1 (Fev) known to express in raphe serotonin neurons (Hendricks et al., 1999); (3) the plasma membrane serotonin transporter (Sert), which recycles released serotonin back to presynaptic terminals of serotonin neurons, and (4) vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (Vmat2), which transports serotonin (and other monoamines) from presynaptic cytoplasm to synaptic vesicles (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: 999 MR and DR serotonin neurons comprised 11 clusters.
source: These 999 MR and DR serotonin neurons comprised 11 clusters (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B based on clustering analysis of scRNA-seq data.

claim: Each cluster contained cells from both sexes after removing genes located on the Y chromosome, indicating that there were few sex-specific differences at the level of transcriptomic clusters.
source: Each cluster contained cells from both sexes after removing genes located on the Y chromosome, indicating that there were few sex-specific differences at the level of transcriptomic clusters (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: No substantial batch effect was observed.
source: No substantial batch effect was observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Six clusters (Cluster 1–6) consisted of only serotonin neurons dissected from the pDR.
source: Of the 11 transcriptomic clusters, six (Cluster 1–6) consisted of only serotonin neurons dissected from the pDR.
evidence: This is based on the dissection strategy and clustering results.

claim: The distribution of markers for Clusters 1–6, Ret, Trh, Gad1, Npas1, Syt2, and C1ql2, were mostly restricted to the pDR.
source: Specifically, we found that the distribution of markers for Clusters 1–6, Ret, Trh, Gad1, Npas1, Syt2, and C1ql2 (Figure 1D), were mostly restricted to the pDR.
evidence: This is based on HCR-smFISH experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: The two common Cluster 7 markers Tacr3 and Met were both highly concentrated in serotonin neurons under the aqueduct in the cDR.
source: The two common Cluster 7 markers Tacr3 and Met were both highly concentrated in serotonin neurons under the aqueduct in the cDR.
evidence: This is based on HCR-smFISH experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Dlk1 expression was found in both the DR and MR, suggesting that Cluster 8 serotonin neurons are located in the MR.
source: Dlk1 should be expressed in the DR clusters as well as Cluster 8 (Figure 1D), and its expression was found in both the DR and MR, suggesting that Cluster 8 serotonin neurons are located in the MR.
evidence: This is based on HCR-smFISH experiments and expression patterns shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Clusters 9–11 markers Irx2 and Piezo2 were mostly found in the MR.
source: Clusters 9–11 markers Irx2 and Piezo2 were mostly found in the MR.
evidence: This is based on HCR-smFISH experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Trh+, Gad1+, and Gad2+ serotonin neurons were mainly located in the dorsal DR.
source: Within the DR, Trh+, Gad1+, and Gad2+ serotonin neurons were mainly located in the dorsal DR, whereas Slc17a8+ (also known as Vglut3, used hereafter) and Syt2+ serotonin neurons were mainly located in the ventral DR and cDR.
evidence: This is based on HCR-smFISH experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Vglut3+ and Syt2+ serotonin neurons were mainly located in the ventral DR and cDR.
source: Within the DR, Trh+, Gad1+, and Gad2+ serotonin neurons were mainly located in the dorsal DR, whereas Slc17a8+ (also known as Vglut3, used hereafter) and Syt2+ serotonin neurons were mainly located in the ventral DR and cDR.
evidence: This is based on HCR-smFISH experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Cluster 6 marker Npas1+ was largely excluded from the densest portion of Tph2 expression at the midline and instead was found scattered in the more rostral and ventral portion of the lateral wings.
source: Cluster 6 marker Npas1+ was largely excluded from the densest portion of Tph2 expression at the midline and instead was found scattered in the more rostral and ventral portion of the lateral wings.
evidence: This is based on HCR-smFISH experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Crhr2 was localized preferentially near the midline and was absent from the lateral wing.
source: On the other hand, Crhr2, which should be expressed in all DR serotonin neuron clusters except Cluster 1 and 6 (Figure 1D), was localized preferentially near the midline and was absent from the lateral wing.
evidence: This is based on HCR-smFISH experiments and expression patterns shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Cluster 6 likely corresponds to serotonin neurons located preferentially in the lateral wings.
source: Thus, Cluster 6 likely corresponds to serotonin neurons located preferentially in the lateral wings.
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial distribution of Npas1+ and Crhr2 expression patterns.

claim: The anatomical organization of the molecular features that define MR clusters is less obvious and different clusters appear more intermingled.
source: In contrast to DR, the anatomical organization of the molecular features that define MR clusters is less obvious and different clusters appear more intermingled.
evidence: This is based on observations from HCR-smFISH experiments.

claim: The majority of the clusters express Slc17a8, which encodes vesicular glutamate transporter-3 (Vglut3).
source: The majority of the clusters express Slc17a8, which encodes vesicular glutamate transporter-3 (Vglut3).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1D and Figure 4.

claim: Almost all serotonin neurons from the cDR express Vglut3.
source: These include almost all serotonin neurons from the cDR, the majority from MR clusters (Domonkos et al., 2016), and DR-3–6 clusters (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1D and supported by citation to Domonkos et al., 2016.

claim: Glutamate is the most prevalent co-transmitter for serotonin neurons.
source: These observations suggest that glutamate is the most prevalent co-transmitter for serotonin neurons.
evidence: This is inferred from the widespread expression of Vglut3 across clusters.

claim: Glutamate co-release from Vglut3+ serotonin terminals has been reported at the hippocampus, orbital prefrontal cortex, nucleus accumbens, ventral tegmental area, and basolateral amygdala.
source: Glutamate co-release from Vglut3+ serotonin terminals has indeed been reported at the hippocampus (Varga et al., 2009), orbital prefrontal cortex (Ren et al., 2018), nucleus accumbens (Liu et al., 2014), ventral tegmental area (Wang et al., 2019), and basolateral amygdala (Sengupta et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Varga et al., 2009; Ren et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2019; Sengupta et al., 2017.

claim: Three DR clusters express Gad1 and Gad2, which encode biosynthetic enzymes for the neurotransmitter GABA.
source: Three DR clusters express Gad1 and Gad2, which encode biosynthetic enzymes for the neurotransmitter GABA.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1D and Figure 4.

claim: Two MR clusters express Gad2 but not Gad1.
source: Two MR clusters express Gad2 but not Gad1, and cDR expresses neither.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1D and Figure 4.

claim: cDR expresses neither Gad1 nor Gad2.
source: Two MR clusters express Gad2 but not Gad1, and cDR expresses neither.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1D and Figure 4.

claim: Few of the Gad1+ or Gad2+ neurons express vesicular GABA transporter (Vgat).
source: Interestingly, few of the Gad1+ or Gad2+ neurons express vesicular GABA transporter (Vgat, Figure 4A left), which is responsible for transporting GABA into synaptic vesicles for synaptic transmission.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Vesicular monoamine transporters can transport GABA into synaptic vesicles.
source: It has been reported that vesicular monoamine transporters (Slc8a1 for Vmat1; Slc8a2 for Vmat2) can transport GABA into synaptic vesicles (Stensrud et al., 2014), and virtually all serotonin neurons expressed Vmat2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D; Figure 4A left).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Stensrud et al., 2014 and data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and Figure 4A.

claim: Virtually all serotonin neurons expressed Vmat2.
source: It has been reported that vesicular monoamine transporters (Slc8a1 for Vmat1; Slc8a2 for Vmat2) can transport GABA into synaptic vesicles (Stensrud et al., 2014), and virtually all serotonin neurons expressed Vmat2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D; Figure 4A left).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and Figure 4A.

claim: 14% of serotonin neurons do not express any of the gene markers for glutamate or GABA transmission.
source: At the single cell level, 14% of serotonin neurons do not express any of the gene markers for glutamate or GABA transmission.
evidence: This is based on analysis of single-cell expression data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: 65% of serotonin neurons express Vglut3.
source: 65% of serotonin neurons express Vglut3, 35% express either Gad1, Gad2, or both, and 13% express markers for Vglut3 and Gad1 or Gad2 (Figure 4A left).
evidence: This is based on analysis of single-cell expression data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: 35% of serotonin neurons express either Gad1, Gad2, or both.
source: 65% of serotonin neurons express Vglut3, 35% express either Gad1, Gad2, or both, and 13% express markers for Vglut3 and Gad1 or Gad2 (Figure 4A left).
evidence: This is based on analysis of single-cell expression data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: 13% of serotonin neurons express markers for Vglut3 and Gad1 or Gad2.
source: 65% of serotonin neurons express Vglut3, 35% express either Gad1, Gad2, or both, and 13% express markers for Vglut3 and Gad1 or Gad2 (Figure 4A left).
evidence: This is based on analysis of single-cell expression data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The majority of serotonin neurons also co-express neuropeptides.
source: In addition to small-molecule transmitters, the majority of serotonin neurons also co-express neuropeptides (Figure 4A right).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (Trh) is highly expressed in DR-1–3 (14% serotonin neurons).
source: For example, thyrotropin-releasing hormone (Trh) is highly expressed in DR-1–3 (14% serotonin neurons, Figure 1C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Corticotropin-releasing hormone (Crh) is highly expressed in the DR-3 cluster but much less everywhere else (7% serotonin neurons).
source: Corticotropin-releasing hormone (Crh) is highly expressed in the DR-3 cluster but much less everywhere else (7% serotonin neurons).
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Neuropeptide B (Npb) is highly expressed in cDR and MR-4 but much less in pDR serotonin neurons.
source: Neuropeptide B (Npb) is highly expressed in cDR and MR-4 but much less in pDR serotonin neurons.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Galanin (Gal) is highly expressed in pDR and MR-1.
source: Galanin (Gal) is highly expressed in pDR and MR-1 (Fernandez et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on expression analysis and supported by citation to Fernandez et al., 2016.

claim: Many serotonin neurons express multiple neuropeptides.
source: Many serotonin neurons express multiple neuropeptides (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: Each cluster has a distinct expression pattern of neurotransmitter (including neuropeptide) receptors.
source: Each cluster has a distinct expression pattern of neurotransmitter (including neuropeptide) receptors (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Grin3a is mainly expressed in pDR but not MR or cDR clusters.
source: For example, Grin3a, encoding subunit 3A of ionotropic NMDA glutamate receptor, is mainly expressed in pDR but not MR or cDR clusters.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Grik1 is more highly expressed in MR clusters.
source: By contrast, Grik1, encoding subunit 1 of the kainate glutamate receptor, is more highly expressed in MR clusters.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Chrna3 and Chrna4 are more enriched in MR clusters.
source: Chrna3 and Chrna4, encoding subunit α3 and α4 of the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor, are also more enriched in MR clusters.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Clusters MR-4 and cDR have the highest expression level of Chrm1 and Chrm2.
source: Clusters MR-4 and cDR have the highest expression level of expression for Chrm1 and Chrm2, encoding muscarinic acetylcholine receptors.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dopamine receptor D2 (Drd2) is highly expressed in DR-3.
source: Dopamine receptor D2 (Drd2) is highly expressed in DR-3 (Niederkofler et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on expression analysis and supported by citation to Niederkofler et al., 2016.

claim: All serotonin neurons express at least one type of serotonin receptors, with the Gi-coupled Htr1 subfamily in particular Htr1a being the most widely expressed.
source: Finally, all serotonin neurons express at least one type of serotonin receptors, with the Gi-coupled Htr1 subfamily in particular Htr1a being the most widely expressed.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Htr1a is highly expressed in the MR-4 cluster, which does not express other serotonin receptors.
source: Htr1a is highly expressed in the MR-4 cluster, which does not express other serotonin receptors.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Htr5b has the strongest cluster specificity of all the genes encoding serotonin receptors.
source: Of all the genes encoding serotonin receptors, Htr5b has the strongest cluster specificity (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: cDR preferentially expresses at least five neuropeptide receptors: gastric inhibitory polypeptide receptor (Gipr), tachykinin receptor 3 (Tacr3), relaxin family peptide receptor 1 (Rxfp1), calcitonin receptor (Calcr), and opioid receptor mu-1 (Oprm1).
source: Notably, cDR preferentially expresses at least five neuropeptide receptors: gastric inhibitory polypeptide receptor (Gipr), tachykinin receptor 3 (Tacr3), relaxin family peptide receptor 1 (Rxfp1), calcitonin receptor (Calcr), and opioid receptor mu-1 (Oprm1).
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Opioid receptor kappa 1 (Oprk1) is expressed specifically in MR-2.
source: Meanwhile, opioid receptor kappa 1 (Oprk1) is expressed specifically in MR-2.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: MR-3 expresses Tacr3, cannabinoid receptor 1(Cnr1), somatostatin receptor-1 (Sstr1), prolactin-releasing hormone receptor (Prlhr), and neuromedin B receptor (Nmbr).
source: Another neuropeptide receptor enriched cluster is MR-3, expressing Tacr3, cannabinoid receptor 1(Cnr1), somatostatin receptor-1 (Sstr1), prolactin-releasing hormone receptor (Prlhr), and neuromedin B receptor (Nmbr).
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Genes encoding a voltage-gated K+ channel (Kchn8) and mechanosensitive channel (Piezo2) are highly expressed in the MR-4 cluster but exhibit little expression in all other clusters.
source: Notably, genes encoding a voltage-gated K+ channel (Kchn8) and mechanosensitive channel (Piezo2) are highly expressed in the MR-4 cluster but exhibit little expression in all other clusters.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The chemokine ligand-12 (Cxcl12) is preferentially expressed in MR-1.
source: The chemokine ligand-12 (Cxcl12) and cadherin-6 (Cdh6) are preferentially expressed in MR-1 and DR-4 clusters, respectively.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cadherin-6 (Cdh6) is preferentially expressed in DR-4 clusters.
source: The chemokine ligand-12 (Cxcl12) and cadherin-6 (Cdh6) are preferentially expressed in MR-1 and DR-4 clusters, respectively.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Transcription factors have been shown to be the best molecular feature for cell type definition.
source: Transcription factors (TFs) have been shown to be the best molecular feature for cell type definition (Schaum et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schaum et al., 2018.

claim: Bcl11a and Bcl11b are highly enriched in DR-3 and MR-4.
source: For example, Bcl11a and Bcl11b (also named Ctip1 and Ctip2) (Chen et al., 2008; Wiegreffe et al., 2015) are highly enriched in DR-3 and MR-4, respectively.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis and supported by citations to Chen et al., 2008; Wiegreffe et al., 2015.

claim: Nfix and Nfib are preferentially expressed in DR-3.
source: Nfix and Nfib (Bedford et al., 1998) are preferentially expressed in DR-3.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis and supported by citation to Bedford et al., 1998.

claim: Irx2 is specific to MR-2 and MR-3.
source: Irx2 (Wylie et al., 2010) is specific to MR-2 and MR-3.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis and supported by citation to Wylie et al., 2010.

claim: Sox13 is highly enriched in cDR.
source: Sox13 is highly enriched in cDR.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Sox14 is expressed in Clusters 1 and 2 in adult serotonin neurons that co-express Gad1 and Gad2.
source: Interestingly, Sox14, previously reported to be associated with GABAergic neurons in developing brain (Lahti et al., 2016), is expressed in Clusters 1 and 2 in adult serotonin neurons that co-express Gad1 and Gad2.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis and supported by citation to Lahti et al., 2016.

claim: Zeb2 is uniquely expressed in cDR and MR-4.
source: Zeb2 (Okaty et al., 2015) is uniquely expressed in cDR and MR-4.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis and supported by citation to Okaty et al., 2015.

claim: Npas1 and Npas3 are preferentially expressed in DR-6.
source: TFs associated with neurodevelopmental disorders, such as Npas1 and Npas3 (Erbel-Sieler et al., 2004), are preferentially expressed in DR-6, and Aff2 (Mondal et al., 2012) is enriched within DR-3.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis and supported by citation to Erbel-Sieler et al., 2004.

claim: Aff2 is enriched within DR-3.
source: TFs associated with neurodevelopmental disorders, such as Npas1 and Npas3 (Erbel-Sieler et al., 2004), are preferentially expressed in DR-6, and Aff2 (Mondal et al., 2012) is enriched within DR-3.
evidence: This is based on expression analysis and supported by citation to Mondal et al., 2012.

claim: Pax5 and Sox14 strongly correlate with Gad1, Gad2, and Trh among dorsal pDR markers.
source: Among dorsal pDR markers we identified Pax5 and Sox14 to strongly correlate (rp >0.5) with Gad1, Gad2, and Trh, among other genes.
evidence: This is based on gene co-expression analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Crhr2 is highly correlated with several TFs, receptors, and neurotransmitter-related genes, most notably Vglut3 and Hcrtr2 among ventral pDR markers.
source: Among ventral pDR markers, we found Crhr2 to be highly correlated with several TFs, receptors, and neurotransmitter-related genes, most notably Vglut3 (Slc17a8) and Hcrtr2.
evidence: This is based on gene co-expression analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Crhr2+ serotonin neurons could use TFs Esr2 and Sox1 to maintain their subtype identity.
source: These Crhr2+ serotonin neurons could use TFs Esr2 and Sox1 to maintain their subtype identity.
evidence: This is inferred from gene co-expression analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Npas3 is specifically expressed in the DR-6 cluster and is highly correlated with Htr1d.
source: Npas3 is specifically expressed in the DR-6 cluster and is highly correlated with Htr1d, suggesting a critical role of maintaining the characteristics of DR-6 serotonin neurons.
evidence: This is based on gene co-expression analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The expression of a large number of cell adhesion molecules, receptors, ion channel proteins and neuropeptides strongly correlate with the expression of TFs Zeb2, Pou3f1, Irx2, and Zfp536.
source: Particularly, the expression of a large number of cell adhesion molecules, receptors, ion channel proteins and neuropeptides strongly correlate with the expression of TFs Zeb2, Pou3f1, Irx2, and Zfp536.
evidence: This is based on gene co-expression analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: 98.5% GFP+ neurons are Tph2+ and 100% Tph2+ neurons are GFP+ in Sert-Flp mice crossed with H11-CAG-FRT-stop-FRT-EGFP mice.
source: Anti-Tph2 staining on the brain slices containing pDR showed that 98.5% GFP+ neurons are Tph2+ and 100% Tph2+ neurons are GFP+ (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5B based on immunostaining experiments.

claim: All GFP-labeled neurons are Tph2+ in mice triple transgenic for Vglut3-Cre, Sert-Flp, and the IS reporter.
source: Anti-Tph2 staining showed that all GFP-labeled neurons are Tph2+ (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C based on immunostaining experiments.

claim: All GFP-labeled neurons are Tph2+ in mice triple transgenic for Gad2-Cre, Sert-Flp, and the IS reporter.
source: Anti-Tph2 staining showed that all GFP-labeled neurons are Tph2+ (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5D based on immunostaining experiments.

claim: Vglut3+ serotonin neurons were mainly located ventrally in the pDR.
source: In the pDR, Vglut3+ serotonin neurons were mainly located ventrally, whereas Gad2+ serotonin neurons were mainly located dorsally, consistent with our previous study (Ren et al., 2018) and the HCR-smFISH results (Figure 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C and supported by citation to Ren et al., 2018 and HCR-smFISH results in Figure 2.

claim: Gad2+ serotonin neurons were mainly located dorsally in the pDR.
source: In the pDR, Vglut3+ serotonin neurons were mainly located ventrally, whereas Gad2+ serotonin neurons were mainly located dorsally, consistent with our previous study (Ren et al., 2018) and the HCR-smFISH results (Figure 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5D and supported by citation to Ren et al., 2018 and HCR-smFISH results in Figure 2.

claim: 98.2% GFP+ neurons were Tph2+ after injection of AAV-CreON/FlpON-mGFP into pDR of either Vglut3-Cre;Sert-Flp or Trh-Cre;Sert-Flp mice.
source: Anti-Tph2 staining showed that 98.2% GFP+ neurons were Tph2+.
evidence: This is based on immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 6B and 6C.

claim: Vglut3+Sert+ GFP cells were mostly located in the ventral pDR.
source: As predicted, Vglut3+Sert+ GFP cells were mostly located in the ventral pDR (Figure 6B), whereas Trh+Sert+ cells were located in the dorsal pDR (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Trh+Sert+ cells were located in the dorsal pDR.
source: As predicted, Vglut3+Sert+ GFP cells were mostly located in the ventral pDR (Figure 6B), whereas Trh+Sert+ cells were located in the dorsal pDR (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6C.

claim: No mGFP+ cell bodies or fibers were found after injection of AAV-CreON/FlpON-mGFP into mice carrying only the Sert-Flp transgene or only the Vglut3-Cre transgene.
source: As negative controls, we injected the same virus into mice carrying only the Sert-Flp transgene or only the Vglut3-Cre transgene and did not find any mGFP+ cell bodies or fibers (n = 3 for each; data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as a negative control result.

claim: Serotonin axons from Vglut3+ population preferentially targeted cortical regions.
source: We found that serotonin axons from Vglut3+ population preferentially targeted cortical regions (Figure 6D), consistent with our previous results (Ren et al., 2018).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6D and supported by citation to Ren et al., 2018.

claim: No GFP-labeled axons were observed in the cortical regions from Trh-Cre;Sert-Flp mice.
source: By contrast, no GFP-labeled axons were observed in the cortical regions from Trh-Cre;Sert-Flp mice.
evidence: This is based on examination of tissue sections shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Trh+ serotonin axons project to the anterior and medial hypothalamus, posterior amygdala, and the lateral geniculate nucleus in the thalamus.
source: Instead, Trh+ serotonin axons project to the anterior and medial hypothalamus, posterior amygdala, and the lateral geniculate nucleus in the thalamus, none of which were targeted by Vglut3+ axons (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Vglut3+ axons preferentially innervate anterolateral cortical regions and adjacent structures such as olfactory bulb, agranular insular cortex, endopiriform, piriform, and claustrum as well as other cortical regions such as entorhinal, primary motor, and barrel cortices.
source: Whole-brain quantitative and statistical analyses showed Vglut3+ axons preferentially in anterolateral cortical regions and adjacent structures such as olfactory bulb, agranular insular cortex, endopiriform, piriform, and claustrum as well as other cortical regions such as entorhinal, primary motor, and barrel cortices.
evidence: This is based on whole-brain imaging and quantification shown in Figure 7.

claim: Trh+ axons were largely absent from anterolateral cortical regions and adjacent structures.
source: By contrast, Trh+ axons, which originated preferentially from the lateral wing of pDR, were largely absent from these structures.
evidence: This is based on whole-brain imaging and quantification shown in Figure 7.

claim: Subcortical regions primarily in thalamus (zona incerta and medial geniculate) and hypothalamus (anterior and dorsomedial nuclei) were preferentially targeted by Trh+ axons and largely avoided by the Vglut3+ population.
source: Conversely, subcortical regions primarily in thalamus (zona incerta and medial geniculate) and hypothalamus (anterior and dorsomedial nuclei) were preferentially targeted by Trh+ axons and largely avoided by the Vglut3+ population (Figure 7E; Figure 7—Video 1).
evidence: This is based on whole-brain imaging and quantification shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The cell bodies of 50 reconstructed serotonin neurons covered large regions of the DR.
source: The cell bodies of these 50 serotonin neurons covered large regions of the DR (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B), and their projections collectively innervated the majority of the brain regions (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C), suggesting their broad coverage of DR serotonin neuron types.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The projections of 50 reconstructed serotonin neurons collectively innervated the majority of the brain regions.
source: The cell bodies of these 50 serotonin neurons covered large regions of the DR (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B), and their projections collectively innervated the majority of the brain regions (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C), suggesting their broad coverage of DR serotonin neuron types.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The projection pattern of individual DR serotonin neurons was highly diverse yet follow some general patterns.
source: Complete morphological reconstruction revealed that the projection pattern of individual DR serotonin neurons was highly diverse yet follow some general patterns (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of 50 reconstructed neurons shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The total axon length of DR serotonin neurons exhibited considerable heterogeneity, from 1.9 cm to 26.3 cm.
source: We found that the total axon length of these DR serotonin neurons exhibited considerable heterogeneity, from 1.9 cm to 26.3 cm.
evidence: This is based on quantification of 50 reconstructed neurons.

claim: Cortex-projecting serotonin neurons had the longest axons.
source: When examined across the six groups, cortex-projecting serotonin neurons indeed had the longest axons (Figure 8H).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8H based on quantification of axon lengths.

claim: The longest axon from a single serotonin neuron (26.3 cm) is >10 times the length of a mouse brain in the longest dimension from rostral olfactory bulb to caudal brainstem.
source: The longest axon from a single serotonin neuron (26.3 cm) is >10 times the length of a mouse brain in the longest dimension from rostral olfactory bulb to caudal brainstem.
evidence: This is based on measurement of the longest reconstructed axon.

claim: There is a general segregation of cortical- and subcortical-projecting serotonin neurons.
source: First, there is a general segregation of cortical- and subcortical-projecting serotonin neurons. Of the 46 forebrain-projecting DR serotonin neurons, 34 have a strong preference (>80% forebrain-projecting axon length) for innervating either cortical or subcortical regions.
evidence: This is based on analysis of 50 reconstructed neurons.

claim: Most of the serotonin neurons tend to focus a majority of their arborization within one brain region.
source: Second, most of the serotonin neurons tend to focus a majority of their arborization within one brain region (e.g., prefrontal vs. entorhinal cortex, Figure 8B; CeA vs. cortical amygdala (CoA), Figure 8—figure supplement 4A3).
evidence: This is based on analysis of 50 reconstructed neurons shown in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 4.

claim: The subcortical-projecting serotonin neurons appear to have more specificity, with most neurons exhibiting dense arborization in one or two nuclei.
source: The subcortical-projecting serotonin neurons appear to have more specificity, with most neurons exhibiting dense arborization in one or two nuclei.
evidence: This is based on analysis of 50 reconstructed neurons.

claim: The cortical-projecting serotonin neurons can have elaborate arborization patterns across multiple cortical areas.
source: The cortical-projecting serotonin neurons can have elaborate arborization patterns across multiple cortical areas (e.g., Figure 8—figure supplement 1C) and the longest total axon lengths per cell (Figure 8H).
evidence: This is based on analysis of 50 reconstructed neurons shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C and Figure 8H.

claim: Most projections of the DR serotonin neurons were unilateral (37/50).
source: While most projections of the DR serotonin neurons were unilateral (37/50), one of the thalamus-projecting neurons had symmetrical bilateral projections in the thalamic target (Figure 8—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is based on analysis of 50 reconstructed neurons.

claim: The cell body locations of traced neurons were consistent with previous results as well as single-cell transcriptome, HCR-smFISH, and whole-brain bulk tracing data.
source: The cell body locations of these traced neurons (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B) were consistent with our previous results (Ren et al., 2018) as well as single-cell transcriptome, HCR-smFISH, and whole-brain bulk tracing data.
evidence: This is based on comparison of cell body locations shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B with previous data.

claim: Cortex-projecting serotonin neurons were biased towards ventral pDR (14 out of 17 cells).
source: Specifically, cortex-projecting serotonin neurons were biased towards ventral pDR (14 out of 17 cells), whereas amygdala-projecting ones were preferentially distributed in the dorsal pDR (3 out of 4 cells).
evidence: This is based on analysis of cell body locations of 50 reconstructed neurons.

claim: Amygdala-projecting serotonin neurons were preferentially distributed in the dorsal pDR (3 out of 4 cells).
source: Specifically, cortex-projecting serotonin neurons were biased towards ventral pDR (14 out of 17 cells), whereas amygdala-projecting ones were preferentially distributed in the dorsal pDR (3 out of 4 cells).
evidence: This is based on analysis of cell body locations of 50 reconstructed neurons.
